comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks an axis damper for repeatable non-bottoming stops; pr-1984 clamps wood in a vise and performs an unguided cut to length.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses a hex key and fine collar adjustment with iterative impact observation. pr-1984 turns a vise handwheel, stabilizes stock, and executes sustained saw strokes along a measured cut line.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate evaluates two dynamic stops, stroke, impact energy/velocity, rebound, overload, and setting retention. pr-1984 requires exactly two wood pieces, a 150 ± 1 mm retained length, specified vise closure and screw rotation, ≤3 mm stock displacement, and saw clearance. Candidate rubric lacks numeric rebound, overload, collar-drift, and locking-torque limits.
comparison.reason: The common screw-turning primitive does not make dynamic shock-absorber commissioning equivalent to forceful clamping and material removal with geometric cut accuracy.
